messages.subject: Re: Percentage of correctly paired fragments
messages.body_plain:
Hi Guillermo Lopez,

Although your mapping percentage is a bit lower than the average I have typically seen (around 80 to 90 percent), I wouldn't say this is unusual. I do see quite a few datasets with mapping percentages similar to yours.

For the percentage of reads assigned to features, I typically see around 50 to 70 of reads successfully assigned. So your assignment rate looks fine.

Best wishes,
Wei

messages.subject: Re: Unexpected zero read counts from featureCounts "-t" argument
messages.subject_clean: Unexpected zero read counts from featureCounts "-t" argument
messages.body_plain:
Hi Chia-Yi,

The reason is that your annotation includes duplicated exons (or exons overlapping with each other). FeatureCounts does not count any read that overlaps with more than one feature by default.

If you add '-O' option to your command, you will then find all your exons have counts. The '-O' option instructs featureCounts to assign a read to all its overlapping features.

Best,

Wei

messages.subject_clean: Unexpected zero read counts from featureCounts "-t" argument
messages.body_plain:
Hi Chia-Yi,

Take exon 2 for example, you have two copies of this exon in your annotation: 2a and 2b. For the reads mapping to exon 2, featureCounts found that they overlap with two exons and therefore it does not count them at all.

If you want to get counts for exons 2, 3 and 4, you will need to keep only one copy for each of them in your annotation.

Cheers,
Wei

messages.subject: Alignment of indels
messages.body_plain:
<https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/-nSxkisZ_cBw/Vsv8-Jo212I/AAAAAAAAAkc/91DF3C0uNEo/s1600/Capture.JPG>
Hi,

I have been trying to test the ability of various sequence aligners to align reads containing indels to genomic DNA. As a test example, I have been using an insertion in an enhancer of the TAL1 gene described in a number of leukemic cell lines (www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/25394790 <http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/25394790>) and I have been using the MOLT3 H3K27ac data from the same paper.

So far I have tested a number of algorithms including BWA, GSNAP and subread. Of the three algorithms, only GSNAP has so far been able to detect a single read containing an 'AC' insertion corresponding to that reported in the paper (see attached IGV screenshot - subread alignment is in the top panel and GSNAP in the bottom panel). A clear visual description of the insertion can be seen in Figure 1 of the above paper (https://d2ufo47lrtsv5s.cloudfront.net/content/sci/346/6215/1373/F1.large.jpg).

I don't actually know exactly how many reads should be mapping to the insertion. However, it is clear that based on the subread parameters I've used (subread-align -T 12 -I 20 -u -t 1 -i hg19 -r $file -o ../bam/$tmp"_H3K27ac_subread.bam") it is currently not picking up at least one read with the indel that was found by GSNAP.

I am wondering if you have any advice regarding parameters that might help subread detect reads with the indel or soft-clipped reads containing the indel? I would prefer to use subread because it is many times faster than GSNAP.

Thank you for your time. Any help would be very much appreciated.

Jason

messages.subject: Re: Alignment of indels
messages.body_plain:
Hi Jason,

Thanks for providing further information. To detect an indel, Subread needs to have at least one read that contains perfected matched 16bp mers at both sides of the indel. For the insertion you are interested in, the number bases at its left side in each read are too short (<16bp) and therefore Subread cannot detect them.

If you can increase your sequencing depth (eg. by merging together the replicates if you have), Subread might be able to detect it if Subread can find a read which includes matched 16 mers flanking the indel from both sides.

The reason why Subread requires the presence of 16bp mers flanking each indel is to ensure a high accuracy for its indel calling.

Best,
Wei
